## 2. Symptom (observable) + reproducibility profile
- HLK **"Connected Standby IO Stress"** (8 hr, Driver Verifier on) fails with **"Multiple BSOD"** `[confirmed]`.
- Bugchecks observed: **`UNEXPECTED_STORE_EXCEPTION (0x154)`** and **`KERNEL_DATA_INPAGE_ERROR (0x7A)`** `[confirmed, Comment 3]`. **No dumps generated** — storage not responding at failure.
- Failure lands **during S0ix entry or exit**; OS recovery succeeds a few times, then a later recovery fails → **soft hang or bugcheck** `[confirmed, Comment 10]`.
- **Heisenbug:** with **WinDbg attached, passes 3/3**, no dumps collectible; one soft-hang seen after detaching `[confirmed, Comments 3–5]`.
- **Reproducibility gates (all [confirmed], Comment 10):**
  - UFS = **primary** storage (NVMe-primary + UFS-secondary → **no repro**).
  - **Windows 25H2** only (24H2 clean).
  - Clean OS **+ Gfx + Wifi** drivers installed (clean OS alone → no CS asserted → no repro).
  - Failure rate **100%** in the failing HLK config (ticket header).

## 3. Initial triage — first discriminators
- **Rule-in (it IS this):** HLK CS IO-stress on **UFS-primary / Win25H2**; a **SCSI READ(06)** hits a **10 s unit-timeout** (`SRB.TimeOutValue = 0xa`); FTH/VISA show the READ **never reached the UFS IP**; OS runs a **hierarchical reset** (`storufs!UfsResetBus` → `storport!RaidAdapterResetBus`); recovery **fails on the SK hynix** device.
- **Rule-out (it is NOT this) — state the exact condition:**
  - Needs PKGC? **NO** — repros with **PKGC disabled** `[confirmed, Comment 10 #5]`. **← key discriminator vs Pattern P1 (`ufs-fabric-timeout-on-pkgc`, 16027585017), which is PKGC-gated.**
  - Boot-time PMC-stuck / IP_ready? **NO** — not a boot/fuse-pull hang → **not P2** (`ufs-fusepull-cdc-race-on-boot`, 16029205689).
  - UFS PHY marginality? **NO** — repros at **0 dB, −3.5 dB, −6 dB** CTLE equalization `[confirmed, Comment 9]`.
  - UFS PGCB sequencing? **NO** — repros with PMC PGCB WA at **20 ms / 30 ms** `[confirmed, Comment 9]`.
  - Link-gear marginality? **NO** — repros at **Gear 3** as well as Gear 4 `[confirmed, Comment 10 #6]`.
  - UFS HW hang? **NO** — UFS resumes normally after the eng-driver breakpoint releases `[confirmed, Comment 11]`.
  - Known **LPSS / bugcheck-`0x9F`** issue? **NO** — removing the **LPSS driver** (to rule out the known `9F` UFS issue) still repros (`0x154`); one setup also **hung at `01CS` post code** `[confirmed, Comment 3]`.
- **Nearest look-alike:** P1 — same platform/UFS-primary/S0ix surface and the same `storufs!UfsResetBus` OS reset path, but **P1 needs PKGC and shows `IS_` SBFES/HBFES OCP-fabric errors**, whereas this repros PKGC-off with the transaction **lost above PSF0 and no fabric error**. **Deciding tell:** PKGC-disabled still fails **and** VISA@PSF4/PSF0 shows **no** UFS-side transaction/error.

## 4. Reproduction recipe (config, images, IFWI, knobs, operating point)
- **Board:** WCL DDR5 SODIMM T3 RVP1. **BKC:** `WCL-25H2-CONS-PROD-25.49.3.16`.
- **IFWI:** `WILDCATLAKEN.0.WCLN.2025.49.2.01` (A1). **BIOS:** `WCL_BIOS_3463_04`. **FSP:** `02.01.025.4750`.
- **UFS devices:** SK hynix **HN8T15DEHKX075** (256 GB) — **fails**; Samsung **KLUEG8UHGC-B0E1** — **recovers**.
- **OS:** Windows **25H2** `26200.7309`; **Gfx + Wifi drivers installed**; **UFS = primary**.
- **Test:** HLK **Connected Standby IO Stress**, Driver Verifier on, 8 hr — three concurrent workloads:
  - **RapidFileVerify** (1M file, Read/Verify enabled),
  - **ConnectedStandby** (random dwell 3/10/25/30/60/75/300/3000 s),
  - **SCSICompliance** (Inquiry, TestUnitReady, RequestSense, Read6/10/16, ReadCapacity10/16, StartStopUnit, SynchronizeCache10, ModeSense6/10, ModeSelect6/10, Reserve6/10, Release6/10).
- **Expect:** during an S0ix transition a SCSI READ times out (10 s) → OS recovery → after a few successful recoveries a **soft hang / BSOD**.
- **Mitigation to avoid repro:** none clean pre-fix; the MSFT private driver (§8) removes the soft hang.

## 5. Fault evidence & instrumentation (machine-readable evidence map)

### 5a. WinDbg — OS reset path `[confirmed, Comments 8 & 11]`
| command / namednode | field | value @ fault | inference | rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dt SRB _SCSI_REQUEST_BLOCK` | `+0x014 TimeOutValue` | `0xa` (10 s) | SCSI **READ(06)**, QueueTag `0x03` unit-timeout | decisive |
| `kv` stack | call site | `storufs!UfsIntelLkfResetBus → UfsResetBus → storport!RaCallMiniportResetBus → RaidAdapterResetBus → RaidUnitHierarchicalReset → RaidHierarchicalResetWorkRoutine → nt!IopProcessWorkItem` | OS ran full **multi-tier reset** (LUN → abort → device → **bus reset**) | decisive |
| dump `16029462685_UFS` | type | **breakpoint** (eng driver), not a bugcheck | failure caught **at UFS reset**, not a HW fault | useful |

> **Recovery-sequence note `[confirmed, Comment 11]`:** the **abort uses the same SRB → inherits the same 10 s timeout**, so a failing abort just burns another 10 s before escalating. And the OS cannot simply toggle HCE and ring the doorbell — **every HCE toggle must follow `LSS (Link Startup) → PMC to HS-G4 / PWM-G1 → data transfer`** before any new transaction; the driver waits for that reset+link-startup to complete before restarting IO (link state is outside the OS). This is exactly why a device that leaves the link *up* (SK hynix, §5d) derails the recovery.

## 6. Debug flow (diagnostic narrowing)
1. **HW/PHY marginality?** Swept CTLE eq (0/−3.5/−6 dB) and PGCB WA (20/30 ms) → still repro → **ruled out HW/PHY** (§3); pointed to SW/flow.
2. **Device hung?** Eng-driver breakpoint at UFS reset; UFS resumes fine after release → **not a HW hang**; the problem is a **lost SCSI READ** (§5a/§5b).
3. **Where is the READ lost?** FTH + VISA@PSF4/PSF0 show **no txn at UFS**, none pending → **lost above PSF0** (D2D/compute) → **Issue #1**, root cause open (§5c).
4. **Why hang, not retry?** On timeout OS runs **hierarchical reset**; for **SK hynix**, Endpoint Reset leaves **link up / `IS_` clean / `DP=1`**, steering OS onto a path that **doesn't HCE-toggle** → link never re-inits → recovery **spins the UTRLDBR/UTRLCLR loop** (§5b) → **soft hang** → **Issue #2**.
5. **Confirm vendor dependency:** Samsung sets **`IS_.DFES` + link-lost (`DP=0`)** → OS HCE-toggles → recovers (§5d). Difference is the device's reaction to Endpoint Reset → **spec-implementation gap**.
6. **Fix probe:** MSFT **private driver** that **resets controller (HCE toggle) after `DME_ENDPOINTRESET` & `DME_RESET`** → **soft hang no longer reproduces** on Samsung **or** SK hynix (§8).

## 7. Root cause (precise mechanism + class)
- **Issue #2 [root-caused]:** UFS **device reaction to `DME_ENDPOINTRESET` differs by vendor**. **SK hynix** keeps the **link up** with **`IS_` clean (`DP=1`)** after Endpoint Reset, so the Windows `storufs` recovery path **does not toggle HCE / re-init the link** and recovery **fails → soft hang**. **Samsung** reports **link-lost + `IS_.DFES`**, which drives the **HCE-toggle** recovery path (UniPro §8.2.6/§8.2.2) that **succeeds**. → **spec-implementation gap between vendor devices and the OS recovery flow.** Contributing protocol smell in FTH: the recovery path issues **`DME_ENABLE` (UICCMD `0x39`)**, which the IP databook says is **not permitted** `[fth-snap]`. **Fix** = OS-driver change to always **HCE-toggle after `DME_ENDPOINTRESET` & `DME_RESET`**.
- **Issue #1 [open]:** a **SCSI READ(06) is lost above PSF0** (never reaches UFS IP) causing the 10 s unit-timeout that *initiates* recovery. Root cause **unknown**; separate HSD (ID not stated); path suspected D2D boundary / compute die; CFI trace pending.
- **root_cause_class:** Issue #2 → **spec-gap** (device-fw vs OS-recovery); the *fix* lands in the OS driver. Issue #1 → **unknown**.
- **Why the naive recovery derails `[confirmed, Comment 11]`:** after `DME_ENDPOINTRESET`/`DME_RESET` the OS must re-init via **HCE toggle → `LSS → PMC to HS-G4 / PWM-G1 → data transfer`** before any new IO. When SK hynix leaves the **link up + `IS_` clean**, storufs skips the HCE-toggle/LSS path and rings the doorbell against a half-reset link → the UTRLDBR/UTRLCLR spin → soft hang. The fix forces the HCE-toggle+LSS sequence unconditionally.
- **Taxonomy status:** `signature: ufs-recovery-softhang-on-endpoint-reset` and `root_cause_class: spec-gap` are **now added** to `reference/taxonomy.md` and this record is indexed in `issues/index.jsonl`.

### 7b. Fingerprint registers (high level)
- **`HCS.DP` (bit 0)** — `0` Samsung (link lost) vs `1` SK hynix (link retained): the branch selector for the OS recovery path.
- **`IS_.DFES` (bit 11)** — **set on Samsung, clear on SK hynix** after Endpoint Reset: the presence/absence of the fatal-error status is what routes the OS onto the recovering vs hanging path.
- **`IS_.UDEPRI` (bit 1)** — flags the `DME_ENDPOINTRESET` event.
- **`UTRLDBR` (0x58) / `UTRLCLR` (0x5C)** — the doorbell/clear pair the recovery loop pounds.
- **`UICCMD` (0x90) = 0x39 (DME_ENABLE)** — the databook-prohibited command seen during recovery.
- Full bit-level decode (offsets, access, enable bits, spec text) → add to `reference/ufs-glossary.md` and link here.

## 8. Fix & verification (or workaround + status)
- **Issue #2:** **MSFT private/eng driver** — controller reset (**HCE toggle**) inserted after `DME_ENDPOINTRESET` & `DME_RESET` in the recovery flow → **original soft hang not reproduced** on **both** Samsung & SK hynix in HLK `[confirmed, Comment 13]`.
  - **Productization:** under MSFT discussion — they may accept only a **smaller interim change**; tied to the current **"2x2"** driver ask. An **ACPI-based variant** was discussed (Klein) but "does not exist today in any of our platforms."
- **Issue #1:** still **open** — SK hynix vendor engaged to explain device behavior (sync target **WW8.2'2026**); feedback given to MSFT; IOunit-timeout understanding to be **tracked in a separate HSD**.
- **Disposition:** `rnavinku` **closed** the ticket — reported HLK issue RC'd as **spec-implementation gap between vendor devices and OS** `[confirmed, Comment 16]`.

## 9. Retrospective (avoidable? prevention? detection gap?)
- **Dead-ends / false leads (do not rechase):** UFS PHY CTLE eq, PMC PGCB WA, link gear (G3), "UFS HW hung", and **PKGC** (repros disabled) — all disproven (§3).
  - **"UFS flash doesn't respond to UFS bus reset"** (early HW hypothesis, Comment 7) — **contradicted** by Comment 11: UFS resumes fine after the breakpoint releases, so the device is not stuck; the lost READ never reached UFS in the first place.
  - **Known LPSS / `0x9F`** issue — ruled out by removing the LPSS driver; still repros (Comment 3).
  - **Clean OS-from-ISO baseline** (Comment 7) — no repro, but only because CS isn't asserted without Gfx/Wifi drivers; not a fix, just confirms the trigger needs the driver stack.
- **Detection gap:** only surfaces on **Win 25H2** + **UFS-primary** + **Gfx/Wifi drivers** + the exact HLK concurrency (RapidFileVerify + CS + SCSICompliance); clean-OS and manual inbox-driver mimics did **not** repro → put this **specific concurrency** in the default validation matrix.
- **Prevention:** validate **vendor-device Endpoint-Reset behavior** (link-lost + `IS_.DFES` vs link-up + clean) against the OS recovery flow **before** qualifying a new UFS device; add a check that the OS recovery HCE-toggles regardless of device error-status reporting.
- **Observability trap:** WinDbg-attached masks it; use the eng-driver breakpoint at UFS reset to force a usable dump.

## 12. Debug story (conversational narrative for first-time readers)
On a WCL-U (A1) booting from a **SK hynix UFS**, the HLK **"Connected Standby IO Stress"** test kept dying with **"Multiple BSOD"** and no dumps — but only on **Windows 25H2**, only with **UFS as the primary drive**, and **never** when a debugger was attached. Early on the team pulled the **LPSS driver** to rule out a *known* `0x9F` UFS issue — it still failed (`0x154`), so that lead was dead. They also suspected the **UFS flash simply wasn't answering the bus reset** — but that was later contradicted: with an eng-driver breakpoint you could see UFS **resume perfectly** once released, so the device was never stuck. The team then went after the usual UFS power/PHY suspects, but **CTLE equalization sweeps, PGCB timing WAs, a Gear-3 downshift, and even disabling PKGC all still failed** — so this was **not** the PKGC fabric-timeout class we'd seen in 16027585017 (that one is PKGC-gated). An engineering driver with a breakpoint at the UFS reset finally caught a dump: a **SCSI READ(06) had timed out at 10 seconds** (`SRB.TimeOutValue = 0xa`), and **FTH + VISA proved the read never reached the UFS IP** — it was **lost above PSF0**, in the D2D/compute path. The FTH snap shows it plainly: everything "served successfully" up to **+00:01:32.7876**, then **"CHK_BAD : Loop Starts Here,"** then a **~10-second dead gap** to **+00:01:42.7563**, after which the OS spins a recovery loop hammering the **doorbell (UTRLDBR, 0x58)** and **clear (UTRLCLR, 0x5C = 0xFDFFFFFF)** registers and even issues a **DME_ENABLE (UICCMD 0x39) the databook forbids**. (The abort, by the way, reuses the same SRB, so it inherits the *same* 10-second timeout — every failed step costs another 10 s.) That "lost read" (Issue #1) is still unexplained and moves to its own HSD. But the *visible* failure — the **soft hang** — comes from **recovery**: the register snaps show **SK hynix answers Endpoint Reset with the link still up, `IS_` clean, `DP=1`**, so Windows takes a path that **never re-inits the link**; **Samsung drops the link and sets `IS_.DFES`**, so Windows **HCE-toggles and re-inits** and recovers. The reason that matters: a correct recovery can't just toggle HCE and ring the doorbell — every HCE toggle has to walk **Link-Startup → PMC to HS-G4/PWM-G1 → data transfer** before any new IO, and SK hynix's "link still up" tricks the driver into skipping it. A **MSFT private driver that forces an HCE toggle after DME_ENDPOINTRESET/DME_RESET** (i.e. always runs that re-init sequence) made the hang disappear on both vendors. Net: **two bugs in one ticket** — an open "lost SCSI read" above PSF0, and a root-caused **vendor-vs-OS Endpoint-Reset recovery gap**.
